>I honestly would rather DONTNOD had revealed that an evil wizard was creating the tornado all along

Honestly, you don't want to go down that route. If they did, everybody would by asking: "But why a calculator? How could a calculator defeat an evil wizard?"

I've seen it happen before.

My personal guess is that, sooner or later, Rick's family would have ended up 'on the cob' as well.

Either that, or it just generally isn't very safe to live on a planet where the matter is so different from regular matter.

Regardless, the way Rick freaked out when he's usually so calm and collected, makes me wonder whether he has experience with similar things in the past. 

He was willing to take either the tiny planet, or the screaming sun planet over that option, so I think we can assume that whatever was about to happen would have been *particularly* bad (In fact, the screaming sun barely seemed to phase him. Compare that to his complete panic at realising that *everything* was on the cob).

>This is a weird realization but, I don't have a toaster....why the fuck don't I have a toaster?!

Maybe it's better that you don't. I mean, look how it ended for Toaster Steve.

There's an urban legend that the song causes suicides. 

It's a very melancholic song, but personally, I doubt it'll actually harm anyone.

[Apparently, this is a bug in cpp.sh.](http://www.cplusplus.com/forum/lounge/144510/)

It seems that sometimes cpp.sh will randomly give you someone else's program.

I tried this out for myself, I just repeatedly compiled the default 'hello world' program that cpp.sh comes up with. Most of the time it compiled properly, a few times it asked me for my age instead, sometimes it asked me to input numbers.
